To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the toxicity of particles is not predictable from their composition, that surface reactivity is crucial, and that micromorphology is important.

the toxicity of particles cannot be predicted on the basis of their composition alone, that surface reactivity is the key to the pathogenicity and that the pathogenic response is determined by the dose of the reactive surface.

(1) the pathogenic response of cells and tissues to particulate matter is determined by surface properties; (2) the surface properties of particles depend on the thermal and mechanical history; (3) surface properties are modified by contact with the environment, including the biological medium; (4) the dose of particles is best expressed on a per-unit-surface basis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the particle-biological interface in determining the toxicological response.
understanding the role of the surface of inhaled particles in the pathogenicity caused to the lungs by the inhalation and retention of particulate matter.
the elucidation of the role of the surface reactivity of particles in the development of lung disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface reactivity of particulates determines their pathogenicity.
, in addition to the well-known role of particle size, surface reactivity is a crucial determinant of particle pathogenicity.
the pathogenic response is not only related to the bulk chemical composition of the particles but also to the physicochemical properties of the particle surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reactivity of the particle-biological environment interface is the key to understanding the toxicity of inhaled particulates.
surface reactivity of inhaled particles determines their pathogenic response.
, with particles, the dose-response relationships and the pathogenic mechanisms depend on micromorphology and surface reactivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface of a particle, not its bulk, determines the biological reactivity.
the surface of the particles is a major factor in the pathogenicity caused in humans by inhalation of particulate matter.
